definitions.explanation: An official check conducted by police or authorities, typically on roads to inspect vehicles and drivers, or at other locations for security purposes.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}の{検問|けんもん}に{引|ひ}っかかった。
examples.english: I got caught at a police checkpoint.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}は{飲酒運転|いんしゅうんてん}の{検問|けんもん}が{増|ふ}える。
{深夜|しんや}に{車|くるま}を{運転|うんてん}していたら{検問|けんもん}があり、{免許証|めんきょしょう}の{提示|ていじ}を{求|もと}められた。
examples.english: I was driving late at night when I came upon a checkpoint and was asked to show my driver's license.

notes:
USAGE:
{検問|けんもん} refers to official inspections, most commonly police checkpoints on roads. In Japan, police set up {検問|けんもん} to check for drunk driving, unlicensed driving, and other traffic violations, especially during holiday seasons.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {検問|けんもん}に{引|ひ}っかかる (get stopped at a checkpoint)
- {検問|けんもん}を{行|おこな}う (conduct an inspection)
- {飲酒|いんしゅ}{検問|けんもん} (drunk-driving checkpoint)
- {検問所|けんもんじょ} (checkpoint location)

The verb form {検問|けんもん}する means to inspect or question someone at a checkpoint.
